skill.name: codebase-search
skill.description: Search and navigate large codebases with semantic queries, grep patterns, glob discovery, Read workflows, and git history checks.
skill.summary: Guides focused semantic, grep, glob, Read, and git-history searches across large repositories.
skill.author: supercent-io

security_audit.summary: Static analysis flagged Markdown fences, example grep and git commands, reference links, and search strings as risky patterns. Manual review found no evidence of prompt injection, data exfiltration, secret access, or hidden execution; all static findings are false positives. Users should still run any suggested shell searches only in intended repositories.

content.value_statement: Large repositories make code paths and dependencies hard to locate quickly. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through targeted semantic, grep, glob, and history searches.
actual_capabilities: Selects semantic search, grep, glob, or Read workflows based on the question.
Provides search patterns for functions, classes, imports, configuration, errors, and tests.
Guides callsite discovery and dependency tracing across related files.
Supports impact analysis before refactors or feature changes.
Suggests git blame and git log checks for code history context.
limitations: It is a guidance skill and does not provide its own search index.
Search quality depends on available repository tools and query specificity.
Bash and git examples require permission in the active workspace.
It cannot guarantee complete results in generated, vendored, or ignored files.

use_cases.title: Find Bug Origins
use_cases.description: Trace an error message from a report to the files, handlers, tests, and dependencies that may cause it.

use_cases.title: Prepare Refactors
use_cases.description: Locate callsites, imports, tests, and related behavior before changing a shared function or module.

use_cases.title: Learn a Repository
use_cases.description: Map entry points, routes, models, configuration, and documentation when joining an unfamiliar project.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Function
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner search for a known symbol.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find where the function named <function_name> is defined and show the most relevant callers.

prompt_templates.title: Trace a Bug
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate debugging from an observed error.
prompt_templates.prompt: Search for this error message, identify where it is raised, and summarize the code path that triggers it: <error_message>.

prompt_templates.title: Map a Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Map how <feature_name> works from entry point to service, data model, configuration, and tests.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an Impact Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced analysis before changing shared code.
prompt_templates.prompt: Before I change <module_or_function>, find callsites, imports, tests, related configuration, and likely regression risks.

output_examples.output: The response identifies the route, controller, service, model, and tests, then explains how data flows between them.

output_examples.input: What depends on the payment processor?
output_examples.output: The response lists direct callsites, imports, related tests, and configuration references, grouped by subsystem.

output_examples.input: Find why this authentication error appears.
output_examples.output: The response starts from the error string, traces throw sites and callers, and highlights the most likely trigger path.

best_practices: Start with a broad semantic query, then narrow with exact grep searches.
Read surrounding context before drawing conclusions from a matching line.
Check tests and git history when behavior or ownership is unclear.
anti_patterns: Do not assume one search result explains the whole feature.
Do not run broad shell searches outside the intended repository.
Do not ignore ignored, generated, or vendored files without confirming relevance.

faq.question: Does this skill execute code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides search workflows and example commands for tools that the user or agent may run with permission.

faq.question: Can it search without Bash access?
faq.answer: Yes. It can still guide Read, Grep, Glob, and semantic search workflows when those tools are available.

faq.question: Does it require internet access?
faq.answer: No. The workflow is designed for local repository inspection. Reference links are documentation only.

faq.question: Can it find every usage of a symbol?
faq.answer: It can guide thorough searches, but generated, ignored, or dynamically referenced code may need extra checks.

faq.question: Is it useful for unfamiliar codebases?
faq.answer: Yes. It starts with broad conceptual searches, then narrows to files, symbols, tests, and documentation.

faq.question: What tools work best with it?
faq.answer: It works best with semantic search, Grep, Glob, Read, and optional git history commands.
